movesets.name: Phazer
movesets.description:
• With Multiscale's incredible bulk potential and Dragon Tail bypassing Taunt, Dragonite is a unique and very effective phazer that massively ups the danger of entry hazards!

  • Dragon Tail VS. Roar: Dragon Tail is preferred for it disregarding Taunt and providing some good chip damage. However, Roar can phaze out meddlesome Fairy-types and users of Substitute.

  • Entry Hazard Teammates: For this Dragonite to be at its most effective, you'll need some partners to at least set up Stealth Rock. Ting-Lu and Archaludon are particularly bulky examples that pair well, but other options include Landorus-T, Swampert, and Annihilape.

  • Earthquake VS. Iron Head: Earthquake is the most wide-reaching coverage move, ensuring good damage against Normal resistances like Garganacl and Archaludon. If using Roar, Iron Head prevents Levitate Pokemon from completely walling Dragonite, and its flinch rate synergies well with Thunder Wave.

  • Thunder Wave: Dragonite's bulk makes it an ace at spreading paralysis, making it more of a team supporter.

  • Substitute versus Encore: Substitute is a fantastic option against Pokemon with status moves that threaten Dragonite's phazing cycles, such as Garganacl, Porygon2, and Toxapex. Encore won't do as well against these threats but does punish opposing foes carrying Substitute that can be a problem for Dragon Tail along with slower foes that use status moves in general such as Ting-Lu and Ursaluna-B. Encore can even be used over extra coverage if teammates can deal with Fairy-types.

  • Extreme Speed versus Aqua Jet: Extreme Speed's ability to pick off threats is useful, even on defensive variants of this set. Despite being half as powerful, Aqua Jet is still worth considering for its ability to pick off weakened Flutter Mane, which can be difficult for this set to handle due to its power when Multiscale isn't in play.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is a high value item, but it's worth using on Dragonite if using Substitute, as it gives Dragonite a serious chance of passively gaining Multiscale's effect back.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet allows Dragonite to play more passively, punishing Pokemon that rely on contact moves like Choice Item Urshifu-R and Annihilape.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots' Stealth Rock immunity makes Multiscale more flexible, especially if Dragon Tail brings in a threat Dragonite isn't equipped to handle.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 76 Def / 180 Spe with Impish: This spread gives up quite a bit of bulk in exchange for outspeeding Adamant Breloom, while still often mantaining a Substitute against Garganacl's Salt Cure.

  • 252 HP / 124 Atk / 108 Def / 4 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread is optimized for use with Earthquake and Aqua Jet, allowing Dragonite to 2HKO 4 Defense Flutter Mane with that combination of moves without needing to Terastallize. Only Modest Tera Fairy Flutter Mane will have a chance to OHKO through Multiscale.

  • 252 HP / 252 Atk / 4 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread is a far more offensive approach, mainly for use with Extreme Speed to pick off threats more effectively.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Dragonite's defensive typing can be quite helpful against foes like Urshifu-R and Chi-Yu, but some of the huge exploitable weaknesses to Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane will require Terastallization to cover.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy's Dragon immunity gels well with Dragonite and is a great defensive typing in general against foes like Chien-Pao and Urshifu.

  • Steel: Tera Steel is not only an incredible defensive typing that covers much of Dragonite's former weaknesses, but the power boost it provides to Iron Head lets it OHKO all but the most bulky Flutter Mane.

  • Normal: Tera Normal isn't that incredible defensively, but it can be worth it for boosting Extreme Speed's power, letting offensive EV spreads 2HKO Chien-Pao with it.

movesets.name: Paraflinch
movesets.description:
• Paraflinch Dragonite is a defensively oriented Dragonite set that takes full advantage of Terastallization and the element of surprise to cripple and downright defeat numerous Pokemon. Multiscale allows Dragonite to paralyze its foes relatively safely, becoming a massive nuisance for unprepared opponents.

  • Air Slash vs. Iron Head: Air Slash is a more practical move for this set, as it can cover a wider range of Pokemon for at least neutral damage. Air Slash also does not trigger Rocky Helmet and is naturally boosted by Dragonite's STAB. The Iron Head variant of Paraflinch, however, gives Dragonite an easier time against a number of common threats such as Flutter Mane, at the cost of struggling against Gouging Fire before they Terastallize.

  • Encore vs. Substitute: Encore will allow Dragonite to effectively check a wider variety of Pokemon such as Ursaluna-B by locking them into an unfavorable move, giving it a free opportunity to land Thunder Wave on your opponent's switch-in on the following turn. Substitute, on the other hand, will give Dragonite a much easier time dealing with defensive Pokemon that rely on status infliction such as Porygon2 and Dragon Tail Archaludon.

Other Options
  • Waterfall: Waterfall can be a viable option. However, the move is less reliable for the application of this set, as its chance to flinch is 20% as opposed to Air Slash and Iron Head's 30%. It does deal more damage to common Electric-types like Thundurus-T though.
EV and IV Spreads

  • 244 HP / 236 Def / 28 Spe: 52 Speed EVs are the minimum Speed requirement to outspeed paralyzed Iron Bundle that lack Booster Energy.

  • 252 HP / 140 Def / 116 Spe: This is the minimum requirement to outspeed paralyzed Modest Choice Scarf Chi-Yu.

  • 0 Attack IVs: If using Air Slash, 0 Attack IVs are highly recommended for having a high chance of retaining Substitute against STAB Foul Play users such as Porygon2

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: In order for Dragonite to survive multiple turns against the likes of Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane, Terastallizating into a better defensive typing is usually a must.

  • Steel: Steel is a great defensive type that provides resistance to Fairy-type attacks, such as Moon Blast from Flutter Mane. If using the physical set, Tera Steel also provides a significant boost to the damage of Iron Head.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is Dragonite's best option against opposing Dragon-types, such as Roaring Moon and Gouging Fire.

  • Water: Tera Water provides Dragonite with the much-needed defensive versatility to paralyze and wall common threats, such as Chien-Pao and Azumarill. Water is an excellent defensive type in general with its only weaknesses being Electric and Grass.

movesets.name: Defensive Dragon Dance
movesets.description:
• Dragonite's good bulk gives it plenty of chances to set up Dragon Dance, while still providing a solid defensive backbone.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake is a reliable move for covering Steel-types, and Fire-types like Gouging Fire if using Iron Head and Tera Steel.

  • Breaking Swipe: While weak, Breaking Swipe's Attack drop makes it even easier for Dragonite to set up, making it preferred over Dragon Claw.

  • Encore: Encore makes setting up on slower defensive foes such as Corviknight fairly easy, though the lack of coverage makes Terastallizing far more important.

  • Thunder Punch versus Electric Tera Blast: If using Tera Electric, Thunder Punch is a low-power but reliable STAB option. However, while Tera Blast almost certainly requires Dragonite to Terastallize, it does avoid Rocky Helmet chip damage and is a tad more powerful.

Other Options
  • Ice Spinner: Ice Spinner deals massive damage to Landorus-T and other Flying-types, making it a reasonable coverage option to consider if using a Tera type that can deal with Steel-types, like Water or Electric.
Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet lets Dragonite play more passively thanks to the chip damage, and can be paired with Encore to severely punish slower physical attackers like Scizor.

  • Clear Amulet: Clear Amulet stops common Attack debuffers such as Charm Flutter Mane and Intimidate Landorus-T from ruining Dragonite's offenses, making it much harder to cycle around. As a bonus, it also stops Rock Tomb Speed drops from common foes like Ogerpon-H.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Preserving Multiscale even when Stealth Rock is set up can help Dragonite survive attacks in emergencies.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers's passive healing gives Dragonite a better matchup against passive foes it can Encore.

  • Covert Cloak: With Covert Cloak and Encore, Dragonite becomes a very solid check to Garganacl, as well as no longer fearing Breaking Swipe or flinches.

  • Weakness Policy: Since Multiscale makes Dragonite very difficult to OHKO, Weakness Policy is a viable option to turn the tables on foes targeting Dragonite's weaknesses.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 188 Defense / 76 Spe with Impish: This EV spread outspeeds up to Jolly Urshifu after one Dragon Dance, and Iron Bundle after two Dragon Dances.

  • 252 HP / 52 Def / 204 Spe with Jolly: This is the minimum Speed needed to outspeed Timid Iron Bundle after a boost, and it also outspeeds Flutter Mane and Chien-Pao.

  • 252 HP / 140 Defense / 112 Speed with Impish: This spread outspeeds Adamant Roaring Moon, Jolly Garchomp, and Timid Chi-Yu after Dragon Dance, all of which are threats that can easily revenge kill Dragonite once Multiscale is broken.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High / Almost Required: This Dragonite lacks a powerful STAB attack without Terastallization, making it highly recommended. If using Tera Flying with Tera Blast as the only attack, this set will need Terastallization to function.

  • Steel: Tera Steel covers Dragonite's former weaknesses very well, and can still work somewhat well even if not Terastallized thanks to Iron Head, though note it makes this Dragonite much more vulnerable to Urshifu and Ogerpon-H.

  • Flying: With Tera Blast, Tera Flying gives Dragonite a solid mono-attacking option and defensive typing in one, at the cost of almost always needing to Terastallize to function.

  • Electric: Though this requires extra coverage to be viable, Tera Electric shields Dragonite from paralysis, which can be combined with Clear Amulet to ruin more supportive Flutter Mane sets! Being only weak to Ground-type attacks also makes it a solid defensive Tera Type for Dragonite.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy gives Dragonite an excellent mono-attacking Tera Blast that gives it an advantage over other Dragon-types.

  • Water: Tera Water gifts Dragonite a resistance to Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash without being weak to Sacred Sword, plus it pairs well with Waterfall.

movesets.name: Encore Trapper
movesets.description:
• Due to Dragonite's offensive presence and high bulk, many opponents choose to either check it defensively or set up against it to break through Roost + Multiscale. Against either option, Encore can turn Dragonite practically invincible allowing it to reside on the field indefinitely in most cases.

  • Fire Spin: This allows Dragonite to defeat almost any Pokemon universally by simply making full use of its longevity. Trapping an Encore locked Pokemon in the field is also highly valuable. Fire Spin is used instead of Wrap because it affects Ghost-types and doesn't trigger chip damage from Rough Skin and Rocky Helmet.

  • Earthquake versus Iron Head: Earthquake prevents Dragonite from being entirely passive against Archaludon, Gouging Fire, and Flutter Mane. Meanwhile, Iron Head fits using Tera Steel, and does massive damage to Flutter Mane.

  • Draco Meteor: With a Bold Nature, Draco Meteor is a powerful move that can catch opposing Dragon-types off-guard and deal big damage to Ursaluna-B and Urshifu formes.

Items

  • Leftovers versus Heavy-Duty Boots Generally, Leftovers preserves Dragonite’'s longevity best, as it cancels out the damage from Sandstorm and makes timer stall easier. However, the increased usage of entry hazard setters in response to Dragonite makes Heavy-Duty Boots a strong option.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet makes it easier for Dragonite to defeat Pokemon such as opposing Dragonite, Urshifu-R, and Gouging Fire (while Dragonite is Terastallized), and its residual damage can be used to execute a win condition.

  • Covert Cloak: With Covert Cloak, this Dragonite becomes a very effective check to Garganacl, in addition to no longer being vulnerable to flinches from Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash while Terastallizing.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Dragonite's typing does have some fairly exploitable weaknesses that can harm its defensive capability, but an immunity to Toxic Spikes and useful resistances to common attack types such as Ground, Fire, and Fighting mean that Terastallization is not always the right play.

  • Fairy: Due to Dragonite’'s low Speed compared to other Dragon-types, Tera Fairy is a great response against them. This also retains its advantage against Urshifu formes.

  • Steel: Tera Steel massively improves Dragonite's matchups against Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle, at the cost of being even more vulnerable to Salt Cure and Urshifu formes.

  • Water: Tera Water adds a resistance to Ice without losing Dragonite's innate Fire-type resistance, which is helpful against Chien-Pao and Urshifu-R.

  • Poison: The niche Tera Poison gives Dragonite a way to remove its common weaknesses without being vulnerable to Toxic Spikes, while still resisting Fighting unlike Tera Steel.

movesets.name: Double Priority Lure
movesets.description:
• With Flying-type Tera Blast OHKOing physically frail and Flying-weak Pokemon such as Flutter Mane, Ogerpon-H, and Urshifu-R, this set is effective at fooling opponents into thinking that it's Choice Band Dragonite.

  • Aqua Jet: It may seem redundant with Extreme Speed, but Aqua Jet is a key move for picking off weakened Ghost-types, such as Flutter Mane, and surprising Focus Sash Pokemon that might use Tera Ghost to avoid being sniped by Extreme Speed, such as Iron Bundle. This can also work against Chien-Pao, but Icicle Crash's flinch chance makes this rather risky.

  • Earthquake versus Low Kick: Earthquake is the preferred coverage move for dealing big damage against Archaludon and Gholdengo, common responses to a Dragonite locked into Tera Blast. Low Kick trades smacking Gholdengo for revenge killing opposing Tera Normal Dragonite and dealing massive damage to Ting-Lu.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is the best nature for needing less chip damage to revenge kill weakened targets with priority attacks, but Jolly can make sense if outspeeding foes like Modest Gholdengo, Adamant Gouging Fire, and the rare Jolly Breloom is appealing.

  • Tera Dependency - Almost Required: This set is highly reliant on using Tera Blast as a luring tool, so Terastallization should be a top priority for Dragonite.

Items

  • Sharp Beak: Sharp Beak gives Dragonite the most offensive presence with the fewest drawbacks, giving Flying-type Tera Blast just enough of a boost to usually 2HKO Ursaluna-B, or 3HKO defensive variants.

  • Assault Vest: Assault Vest vastly improves Dragonite's matchup against Iron Bundle and Flutter Mane, especially if Multiscale's protection has been lost.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots means Stealth Rock will no longer remove this set's ability to trade blows with powerful threats.

movesets.name: Bulky Offensive Dragon Dance
movesets.description:
• While giving up Extreme Speed and Scale Shot may seem unusual, it allows Dragonite to use both Multiscale and the unpredictability of Terastallization to become an extremely dangerous bulky sweeper that teams often have the wrong response to!

  • Roost: Despite this set's more offensive approach, Roost is still highly recommended for taking full advantage of Multiscale.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head is a good choice if using Tera Steel, but even outside of that, it offers much more damage against Flutter Mane and common Tera Fairy foes like Raging Bolt and Toxapex than Earthquake.

  • Outrage: Outrage has tremendous power compared to any other attack from Dragonite, but Flutter Mane flipping it into a chance to revenge kill means it's best to lock-in late-game when the sweeping shot is clear.

  • Ice Spinner: Ice Spinner works best with Clear Amulet, making sure Landorus-T and Dragonite are easy to break through before they Terastallize.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is usually preferred for the extra damage output, and the given EV spread still outspeeds Adamant Chien-Pao after a Dragon Dance. Jolly is required for outspeeding Timid Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle though.

Other Options

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch is handy for roasting Scizor and dealing good damage to Corviknight, but it can't replace Earthquake, since hitting Archaludon hard is extremely important.

  • Thunder Punch: If using Tera Electric, Thunder Punch is a less risky alternative to Tera Blast in exchange for getting hit by Rocky Helmet. It's best used with Ice Spinner over Earthquake.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick is an easy way to OHKO Chien-Pao compared to Earthquake, but Flutter Mane laughing at it means Iron Head becomes required coverage, and it does less damage to Archaludon than Earthquake.

Items

  • Clear Amulet: Clear Amulet protects Dragonite from Pokemon that can ruin its sweep with Attack debuffs, such as Landorus-T and Charm Flutter Mane, as well as Breaking Swipe users like Gouging Fire and opposing Dragonite.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry is an effective way around common status spreaders like Flutter Mane, Archaludon, and Dragapult.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots ensures that Stealth Rock won't break Multiscale.

  • Rocky Helmet: If using Roost, Rocky Helmet is a good way of punishing Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes if it lacks Punching Glove or if switching into Aqua Jet.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High / Medium: If making use of Tera Blast for Tera types like Flying, Dragonite will usually want to Terastallize as much as possible. Without Tera Blast, it becomes less necessary, but it's still often worth doing due to it making Dragonite a nightmare to OHKO!

  • Flying: Tera Blast Flying offers incredible power with no drawbacks outside of Terastallizing, making it a great choice for sweeping!

  • Steel: Tera Steel is a more defensive approach to this set, covering Dragonite's common weaknesses to Fairy, Dragon, and Rock.

  • Ground: When combined with Clear Amulet, Tera Ground gives Dragonite the tools to defeat common support Flutter Mane moves like Thunder Wave and Charm in addition to a powerful Earthquake.

  • Electric: Tera Electric works great with Ice Spinner covering Landorus-T, giving Dragonite another way to soak up Thunder Wave and even Serperior's Glare!

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy isn't as great defensively for Dragonite as Tera Steel, but the Dragon immunity is great for keeping Multiscale intact, and it makes Dragonite a good check against Urshifu-S.

strategies.overview:
• Dragonite's great movepool, well-rounded stats, great ability in Inner Focus that makes it immune to Fake Out and Intimidate from Incineroar, and stellar matchups into threats like Urshifu-R, Rillaboom, and Ogerpon-W makes Dragonite a great Pokemon in Regulation F.

  • When holding a Choice Band, Dragonite becomes one of the scariest Pokemon in the metagame for its breaking power. Its best partner, Chien-Pao, supports it with Sword of Ruin and pressures Pokemon that prevent Extreme Speed, such as Indeedee and Flutter Mane. Dragonite and Chien-Pao also are good into Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W, making Dondozo and Tatsugiri, which struggle with these two, great partners as well.

  • Flutter Mane is also a great partner, as it breaks through Iron Hands and Gholdengo for Dragonite, while Dragonite is a great switch into Scarf Urshifu-R and Rillaboom.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
• Extreme Speed is a priority move that hits the majority of the metagame for neutral damage, making it ideal to lock into.

  • Aerial Ace allows Dragonite to OHKO Pokemon like Urshifu-R, Rillaboom, and Amoongus without having to be lock into Outrage. Aqua Jet is secondary priority and allows it to double up with its partner on Ghost-types like Flutter Mane, and Ice Spinner allows it to remove Indeedee-F's Psychic Terrain while still having coverage for Pokemon like Rillaboom and Amoongus.

  • Outrage is used as its Dragon-type STAB move and allows it to OHKO almost the entire metagame.

  • Stomping Tantrum gives coverage into Steel-types like Kingambit and Archaludon.

  • The Speed EVs allow Dragonite to outspeed Dragapult in Tailwind, with the remaining EVs maximize its Attack and round out its bulk, allowing it to live attacks such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Dazzling Gleam

  • Normal is used as the Tera type, boosting Dragonite's Extreme Speed to stellar levels of power and removing its weaknesses to common Fairy- and Ice-type moves.

movesets.name: Loaded Dice Sweeper
movesets.description:
• Loaded Dice Dragonite threatens heavy damage and a boost to its Speed with Scale Shot, allowing it to outspeed Adamant Chien-Pao and Modest Flutter Mane. Inner Focus can be used to stop Incineroar from slowing it down, while Multiscale can make it difficult to remove, letting it get a key Scale Shot off.

  • Dragonite is common on teams with partners that make it even harder to remove, especially if it has Multiscale, such as Ting-Lu's Vessel of Ruin weakening foes like Flutter Mane and Raging Bolt, or Sinistcha's Hospitality healing it back to full HP and reactivating Multiscale. Partners that struggle into Incineroar, such as Chien-Pao and Gouging Fire, appreciate Dragonite blocking Intimidate with Inner Focus and threatening it with damage.

  • Scale Shot is Dragonite's strongest Dragon-type attack without risking locking into Outrage. Iron Head can threaten an OHKO on opposing Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and deal large damage to Tera Fairy Raging Bolt after Scale Shot pressures it to Terastallize. Extreme Speed can pick off low-HP targets and beat out other priority moves like Sucker Punch and Thunderclap.

  • Loaded Dice turns Scale Shot into a much more powerful move on average, with four hits OHKOing less bulky variants of Raging Bolt and five hits nearly always securing an OHKO.

  • After a Speed boost from Scale Shot, Dragonite outspeeds most of the unboosted metagame, allowing it to run an Adamant nature to improve damage rolls. Once its Speed is boosted, it can OHKO Focus Sash Chien-Pao with a five-hit Scale Shot and flinch slower foes with Iron Head. An Adamant nature is necessary for OHKOs on bulky Raging Bolt, and a Chien-Pao on the field can further improve damage rolls with Sword of Ruin.

  • Tera Steel turns Dragonite's weaknesses to Dragon-, Fairy-, and Ice-type moves into resistances, helping against Draco Meteor from Raging Bolt, Moonblast from Flutter Mane, and Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao. Additionally, it boosts Iron Head's damage output, guaranteeing an OHKO on bulky Flutter Mane.

strategies.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Dragonite is a very common bulky physical attacker on balance and physically offensive Coaching teams. Dragonite shines particularly well against weakened teams. It also appreciates redirection or speed control to make up for its mediocre Speed. It works well at supporting teams against hyper offensive teams, with its Multiscale sets allowing it to survive attacks from many common wallbreakers, including Garchomp and Kingambit. Dragonite works well on balance teams, which value more the great consistency and versatility in matchups and the support it can provide to the team through Haze and Tailwind.
  • Dragonite works very well in tandem with Gholdengo and Kingambit, which can cover the Fairy- and Ice-types that may threaten Dragonite. Dragonite also appreciates Coaching support from partners such as Sneasler, which can allow it to mitigate Defense drops from Scale Shot and become difficult to remove for many teams with just a few Coaching boosts. Additionally, redirection from Amoonguss and Fake Out from Rillaboom and Incineroar allow it to better fulfill both its offensive and supportive roles on a team.
  • Dragonite's main issues are its relatively low Speed, weakness to Intimidate, and inability to hit Fairy- and Steel-types except with relatively weak coverage options. Therefore, partners like Kingambit and Sneasler can help hit Dragonite's checks heavily. Additionally, Coaching can help shore up its lesser damage output, particularly against Intimidate from Incineroar, and Defiant from the aforementioned Kingambit as well as Annihilape can help punish Intimidate cycling. Another issue for Dragonite are Pokemon that are faster than it and can threaten to OHKO it, such as Dragapult, Alolan Ninetales, and Garchomp. Therefore, redirection is of great use to these Dragonite sets to deal with such threats.

Strategy Comments

  • Dragonite's main role on teams is as a bulky attacker that can also provide support for its team through Haze and Tailwind. It uses its power and priority to clean up weakened teams while maintaining usefulness throughout the game.
  • Dragonite is best used for its heavy damage output and large bulk, so it must be positioned it carefully around potential threats. Dragonite is at its best when Multiscale is kept intact, so keeping it away from weak attacks that may break it is crucial, as having Multiscale can allow Dragonite to tank a powerful hit from a threatening Pokemon and KO back. It can be used as a strong lead into offensive strategies or as a late-game cleaner against more balanced teams. It can also provide important support for its team if it is running Tailwind.
  • Dragonite's biggest issues are against Steel-types that are capable of withstanding its coverage options, such as Gholdengo and Corviknight, and strong Fairy- and Ice-types like Alolan Ninetales. To mitigate these threats, position your other Pokemon that can handle them and hit them with heavy damage early in the game with partners such as Sneasler and Incineroar so Dragonite can pick them off later in the game once correctly positioned. Another way around these threats is with redirection to protect Dragonite or Coaching support so it can overpower its checks.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description:
• Dragonite uses its high Attack and strong defenses, which are further boosted by Multiscale, to be a very powerful bulky physical attacker. It can be used to check a variety of metagame threats, including Sneasler, Rillaboom, and Torkoal, and provide support for itself and its teammates through the likes of Tailwind and Haze.

  • Scale Shot gives Dragonite a consistent and powerful STAB option, and the Speed boost gives it the potential to sweep teams. Tailwind allows Dragonite to support its team through speed control. Extreme Speed gives Dragonite a strong priority option to finish off low HP foes. Additionally, Haze can be used to counter setup sweepers like Dondozo. Ice Spinner provides coverage for Dragon-types with a 4x weakness to Ice such as Garchomp and can be used to clear Terrains, namely Psychic Terrain, from the field, whereas Stomping Tantrum gives it coverage for Steel- and Fire-types such as Kingambit and Incineroar.

  • Tera Fairy gives Dragonite an important immunity to Dragon-type moves, particularly Scale Shot from opposing Dragonite, giving it strong defensive utility and the ability to check powerful Dragons like Garchomp while removing Dragonite's Fairy and Ice weaknesses. Fairy is also a good defensive typing, being neutral or resistant to the majority of metagame-relevant attacks. However, this Tera type can leave it vulnerable to other important attacks, including Dire Claw from Sneasler and Make It Rain from Gholdengo. Tera Steel gives Dragonite a resistance to Ice-, Dragon- and Fairy-type attacks, including Blizzard from Alolan Ninetales, Moonblast from Primarina, and Dragon Claw from Garchomp that threaten it, while providing an immunity to Sneasler's Dire Claw and a resistance to Gholdengo's Make It Rain. This Tera type can also make it vulnerable to Ground-, Fire- and Fighting-type attacks.

  • 52 Speed EVs with an Adamant Nature allow Dragonite to outspeed Dragapult under Tailwind while allowing it to naturally outspeed Rillaboom and Archaludon and Ursaluna-B with low Speed investment while maximizing its damage output and maintaining its massive bulk. This Speed investment should only be used with an Adamant nature; a Jolly nature and maximum Speed investment can be used to increase the scope of things that Dragonite can outspeed after a Scale Shot; an example of a threat that Dragonite now outspeeds is Dragapult.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
Dragonite is an incredible defensive utility Pokemon thanks to its good stats and useful typing that let it check foes such as Landorus, Ogerpon-W, and Ogerpon-H. It also has a good movepool, with Haze and Dragon Tail making for great anti-setup moves and Roost providing recovery for its team; Multiscale also helps to improve the team's defensive capabilities. Dragon Tail and Haze are good against setup sweepers like Iron Hands, Gholdengo, and Swords Dance Ogerpon formes. Dragon Tail is good for accumulating chip damage, especially on entry hazard-stacking teams, while Haze can clear both foes' stat boosts and teammates' Intimidate drops, and it also works against Fairy-types like Primarina and Diancie as well as Tera Fairy users like Archaludon. Iron Head is good against the aforementioned Fairy-types and Alolan Ninetales as well as Chien-Pao. Ice Spinner hits both Landorus formes, as well as clearing Psychic Terrain. Roost helps provide the team with longevity, helping Dragonite fulfill its role as a defensive wall better. The given EV spread allows Dragonite to survive an Adamant Chien Pao's Icicle Crash and a Life Orb Kyurem's Blizzard with Multiscale. Dragonite struggles against foes that can hit it super effectively like Porygon2, Chien-Pao, Primarina, and Raging Bolt. Dragonite also does not like Incineroar, as it can weaken Dragonite's damage output with Intimidate, prevent it from moving with Fake Out, and remove its Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off to prevent it from switching in as often if Stealth Rock is up. Tera Steel grants Dragonite a boost to its Iron Head's damage and allows it to flip the matchup on the aforementioned checks, gaining a resistance to the Ice-, Fairy-, and Dragon-type moves that would otherwise threaten it. However, Tera Steel does worsen the matchup against Incineroar and prevents Dragonite from checking foes that it normally checks, like Landorus and Ogerpon-H.

Notable Partners

Entry Hazard Setters: Teammates like Landorus-T and Ting-Lu make for good partners, as Dragonite can take advantage of their entry hazards and its ability to phaze foes to rack up extra hazard chip damage. In return, Dragonite helps them with the longevity issues they struggle with. Be wary of stacking up Ice-weak teammates when using these partners, as foes like Chien-Pao and Kyurem may become problematic to deal with.

Fire- and Steel-types: Pokemon like Incineroar, Volcanion, and Gholdengo appreciate Dragonite's ability to switch in on the Ground-type moves that threaten them. Dragonite can also provide recovery to the former two, helping them stay on the field for longer. In return, these partners are good against the Ice- and Fairy-types that Dragonite struggles with, and Incineroar can help Dragonite tank physical attacks better thanks to Intimidate, while Gholdengo gives Dragonite a Spore immunity with Good as Gold.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 2 onwards

Price Range: 15-16 points

Overview: Dragonite is a strong, versatile physical attacker that can serve well as a setup sweeper or wallbreaker. Its Multiscale ability provides it with easy setup opportunities and can let it serve as a roadblock to opposing Pokemon, and its wide variety of coverage moves, including strong priority in Extreme Speed, can break holes in an opponent's team. However, Dragonite is harmed by its poor access to STAB moves, mediocre base Speed, reliance on Heavy-Duty Boots to stay at full health, and unfortunate case of four-moveslot syndrome.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Setup Sweeper: Using Multiscale, Dragonite usually gets at least one free opportunity to set up with Dragon Dance. The main decision when building Dragonite for this role is whether to use three attacks, sacrificing recovery and possible additional chances at using Multiscale to set up further, or use two attacks and Roost, gaining that recovery but sacrificing coverage, a STAB move, or priority with Extreme Speed. It can also sometimes use Encore instead of Roost to punish foes and give itself more setup opportunities.

Wallbreaker: In this role, Dragonite uses a Choice Band—or occasionally a special set with Choice Specs—to break the opposing team. Its powerful attacks like Outrage and Earthquake can heavily damage foes, and it can revenge kill or clean up a weakened team with boosted Extreme Speed.

Offensive Utility: Dragonite can use its already-substantial Attack to wear down foes without needing a boost. Its bulk is also solid, and it can stop many Pokemon in their tracks with Multiscale when it is at full health. When acting in this role, it usually uses Roost to restore Multiscale and often takes advantage of utility moves like Thunder Wave and Dragon Tail.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Dragon Claw, Outrage, Scale Shot, Hurricane, Draco Meteor, Air Slash, Dragon Pulse

Setup Moves: Dragon Dance, Agility

Utility Moves: Roost, Substitute, Thunder Wave, Encore, Dragon Tail, Roar, Haze

Coverage: Extreme Speed, Earthquake, Iron Head, Thunder Punch, Fire Punch, Stone Edge, Rock Slide, Ice Spinner, Aqua Tail, Waterfall, Low Kick, Blizzard, Ice Beam, Fire Blast, Flamethrower, Focus Blast, Hydro Pump, Surf, Thunderbolt, Thunder

Niche Moves

Brick Break: Against teams with strong dual screens setters, Dragonite can use Brick Break to remove Reflect, Light Screen, and Aurora Veil.

Aerial Ace: Although normally too weak to be worth running, Aerial Ace is Dragonite's best physical Flying-type STAB move. In matchups where the opposing team is weak to Flying-type moves, Aerial Ace can be adequate once Dragonite is set up with a Dragon Dance or two.

Fire Spin: Using Fire Spin, Dragonite can trap an overly passive foe and set up on it with Dragon Dance or force a switch-in to stay in while it switches to an ally.

Rain Dance: Uncommonly, Dragonite can use Rain Dance to boost the accuracy of Hurricane, get rid of opposing sun, and support teammates.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: On Dragonite sets that rely on Multiscale, Heavy-Duty Boots is often essential to prevent Stealth Rock from damaging Dragonite and bringing it below full HP. Even on less Multiscale-reliant sets, Dragonite appreciates Heavy-Duty Boots removing its weakness to Stealth Rock.

Choice Band: A Choice Band can enhance Dragonite's wallbreaking power. Teams lacking a Dragon immunity can be severely threatened by a Choice Band-boosted Outrage, and Dragonite can revenge kill with its empowered Extreme Speed or clean up weakened teams late-game once any Normal-resistant foes have been KOed or sufficiently damaged.

Leftovers: When its teammates support it with reliable entry hazard removal or the opponent has non-threatening Stealth Rock setters, Leftovers can be used on bulkier Dragonite sets alongside Roost to consistently restore Multiscale.

Lum Berry: As a setup sweeper, Dragonite greatly suffers from status effects. A Lum Berry can cure any status it receives from foes, as well as being able to remove confusion if it runs Outrage.

Niche Items

Weakness Policy: While Multiscale is active, Dragonite is not particularly threatened by most super effective moves, so a Weakness Policy can exploit this to boost its stats.

Choice Specs: Dragonite is viable as a special wallbreaker when the opponent has physical walls that stop it in its tracks, with access to strong special STAB moves like Draco Meteor and Hurricane and coverage options like Fire Blast and Thunderbolt.

Damage-boosting Items: Dragonite's wide variety of coverage makes running damage-boosting items tempting. Silk Scarf is especially good, as it boosts Extreme Speed. However, Dragonite normally prefers not to run Life Orb because it breaks Multiscale.

Loaded Dice: If using Scale Shot, Loaded Dice can make it a more powerful Dragon-type STAB move than Dragon Claw.

Ability Shield: Ability Shield can preserve Multiscale against foes with Mold Breaker or other ability-ignoring options.

Mental Herb: Against foes with Taunt or Encore, Mental Herb can help Dragonite set up without getting disrupted.

Eject Pack: When running Draco Meteor, Eject Pack can allow Dragonite to pivot out once, maintaining momentum after using a powerful attack.

Tera

Dragonite is normally Tera-banned. If it is allowed to Terastallize, it can be an extremely strong and versatile option and likely should be your primary Tera Captain. Tera Normal can boost Dragonite's Extreme Speed to game-winning levels, especially when strengthened by Dragon Dance or Choice Band, while Tera Flying can give it a stronger physical Flying-type STAB move than Aerial Ace. Other Tera types can boost Dragonite's many coverage moves, such as Tera Ground to boost its already-powerful Earthquake and flip its weaknesses to enable it to set up, Tera Steel to resist all its weaknesses and help it avoid status, and Tera Fire to gain an immunity to burn.

Draft Strategy

Dragonite can be a solid wincon with the right support, using Multiscale to be nearly guaranteed a turn of setup with Dragon Dance. Drafts are not often built around it, as it is somewhat flawed in terms of base Speed and access to STAB moves compared to other top-tier wincons, but it can fit onto many rosters looking for a secondary threat. It can also function as an effective wallbreaker with access to a good priority move in Extreme Speed.

Entry Hazard Removal: Partners that can reliably remove entry hazards, such as Iron Treads and Cyclizar, can help with Dragonite's weakness to Stealth Rock and make it less reliant on running Heavy-Duty Boots to preserve Multiscale.

Pivots: Dragonite prefers not to directly switch into attacks, as taking even a little damage breaks Multiscale. Offensive pivots that scare foes out and then use a pivoting move, such as Meowscarada and Iron Bundle, and defensive pivots that can take a hit and then switch, such as Galarian Slowking and Corviknight, can synergize well with Dragonite.

Steel-types: Steel-type Pokemon are excellent partners for Dragonite, as they resist all of its weaknesses and threaten three of them—Ice, Fairy, and Rock—offensively. Scizor, Tinkaton, and Heatran are all very solid in this regard.

Entry Hazard Setting: As a primarily offensive Pokemon, Dragonite appreciates entry hazards like Stealth Rock and Spikes, which make netting KOs easier for it. Hazard setters that pair well with Dragonite include Iron Treads and Skarmory.

Shed Tail: Dragonite is one of the best partners for Shed Tail users like Cyclizar and Orthworm. Being passed a Substitute at full health means that Multiscale reduces damage to both the Substitute and Dragonite itself, giving it an easy opportunity to set up and sweep the opposing team.

Checks and Counters

Physical Walls: Physical walls can often deal with Dragonite, especially ones that resist its Dragon-type STAB moves or aren't threatened by Earthquake. Pokemon like Galarian Weezing, Dondozo, and Rotom-W can wall Dragonite and stop its sweep until they are dealt with. Dragonite can sometimes run special attacks to play around these Pokemon, but its special sets often perform worse than physical sets once the surprise factor is lost.

Ice-type Moves: Ice Beam and Ice Spinner are widely distributed coverage moves that Dragonite has a quadruple weakness to. Pokemon with access to these moves that can outspeed Dragonite or survive its attacks after setting up can spell doom for it. Iron Bundle is a particular terror, often using Booster Energy or Choice Scarf to outspeed Dragonite even after a Dragon Dance, forcing it out with the threat of an Ice Beam and then using the opportunity to pivot out with Flip Turn to keep momentum. Additionally, Pokemon with access to Triple Axel like Weavile threaten Dragonite even more, as Triple Axel breaks Multiscale with its first hit and normally KOes Dragonite with the next two.

Stealth Rock: If Dragonite isn't running Heavy-Duty Boots or its item gets removed with Knock Off, its weakness to Stealth Rock can substantially worsen its performance. Taking damage from Stealth Rock upon entering the field breaks Multiscale and thus removes one of its core strengths.

Status Effects: Being inflicted with status is very bad for Dragonite. It can function around paralysis by increasing its Speed with Dragon Dance and also by using Extreme Speed, but poison breaks Multiscale every turn even if Dragonite recovers with Roost, and burn does the same along with hindering its Attack.

movesets.name: Altarianite
movesets.description: Dragonite is one of the most formidable setup sweepers in the metagame, capable of unleashing incredibly powerful Pixilate-boosted Extreme Speed, further amplified by Dragon Dance. Additionally, it boasts exceptional coverage options to deal with foes that can safely switch into its Extreme Speed. Fire Punch handles Magearna and Corviknight. Alternatively, Earthquake deals more damage to Magearna, Pecharunt, and Garganacl, but is completely walled by Latiasite variants of the former two, as well as setup Corviknight. Waterfall, on the other hand, hits all the aforementioned foes reliably, albeit weakly, along with dealing super effective damage to Ho-Oh and Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk; it can also be used to fish for flinches in dicey situations. Dragonite may also utilize Facade to severely punish attempts to burn it by foes like Milotic, Ho-Oh, and Arceus formes, as well as turn the tables against Gyaradosite Pecharunt when Pecharunt poisons it. Roost is nearly essential to provide Dragonite with reliable recovery. The Speed EVs allow it to outspeed uninvested Manectite Magearna. Dragonite can fit seamlessly into various offense and balance teams, where it can serve as a potent revenge killer and sweeper. Pairing it with entry hazard setters such as Magearna, Great Tusk, and Swampert applies immense offensive pressure on the opposing team as Dragonite spams Extreme Speed. Similarly, hazard removers like Great Tusk and Corviknight are amazing allies, allowing it to avoid getting easily chipped and preventing Multiscale from breaking pre-Mega Evolution. Dragonite is vulnerable to other Altarianite Extreme Speed users, such as Entei, Hisuian Arcanine, and Regieleki, making checks to these like defensive Eternatus and Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk excellent pairing options. Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk also applies pressure on Magearna and Pecharunt, two of Dragonite's most troublesome walls.

movesets.name: Aerilate
movesets.description: Aerilate Dragonite sacrifices its defensive utility to become a more offensively potent setup sweeper; it uses its already good Attack stat boosted by Pinsirite as well as Multiscale pre-Mega Evolution to maul defensive staples like Pecharunt, Hippowdon, and Ho-Oh that Altarianite variants struggle with while still keeping its revenge killing prowess for Urshifu-R and Spectrier. Salamencite is also a usable option if a teammate is already using Pinsirite, as it still gives Aerilate as well as boosting Dragonite's Defense, which can come in handy with setting up. Earthquake lets Dragonite deal with Pokemon like Raging Bolt and non-Latiasite Magearna and Garganacl that would otherwise give Dragonite major trouble. Fire Punch prevents Dragonite from being completely countered by Corviknight and Latiasite Magearna, while Facade allows Dragonite to take advantage of burns from Arceus-Water, Milotic, and Ho-Oh, as well as poison from Pecharunt and Eternatus. If more longevity is required, Roost can be used in order to keep Dragonite healthy in the span of longer games. The Speed EVs allow Dragonite to outspeed Pinsirite Magearna unboosted. Aerilate Dragonite has an amazing offensive presence, but due to its Stealth Rock weakness and overall limited longevity, it is only usable on more offensive teams. Dragonite appreciates entry hazard control from removers like Great Tusk and Regieleki or Sablenite users like Swampert and Magearna, so it doesn't take huge damage from Stealth Rock and can keep Multiscale active before Mega Evolving. Hazard setters like Swampert, Great Tusk, and Magearna help wear down Dragonite's checks like defensive Arceus formes, Great Tusk, and Raging Bolt. They also help in checking Altarianite Extreme Speed users like Hisuian Arcanine, Regieleki, and opposing Dragonite, preventing them from revenge killing it. Pokemon like Entei, Lunala, and Great Tusk can also help in wearing down Dragonite’s checks, as they can break down walls Dragonite heavily struggles with like Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Ho-Oh for it to sweep, and vice versa. Other Pokemon that can deal with the aforementioned walls, like Raging Bolt and Iron Crown, are also greatly appreciated.

movesets.name: Dragon Dance + Z-Move
movesets.description:
Dragonite is an elite offensive Pokemon that can disrupt common balance structures when holding a Z-crystal; common switch-ins to Dragonite like offensive Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Gliscor fall to +1 Devastating Drake. Dragonite also has great defensive utility, using Multiscale to effectively set up Dragon Dance in front of foes such as Ogerpon-W and Urshifu-R. Earthquake grants Dragonite the opportunity to hit Pokemon such as Heatran and Toxapex, which can discourage any Stealth Rock-setting or Haze attempts, respectively. It also threatens other Steel-type Pokemon like Kingambit and Melmetal. Fire Punch discourages bulky Steel-types that don't mind Earthquake such as Ferrothorn, Air Balloon Gholdengo, and Corviknight from coming in freely. A Jolly nature is usually preferred, as it allows Dragonite to outspeed foes like Zamazenta and Tapu Koko at +1.

This variant of Dragonite is found on more offensive structures, where it is paired with Pokemon such as Mega Diancie; it can deny any attempts of entry hazard setting from the opposition, as this Dragonite set lacks Heavy-Duty Boots. Dragonite, in return, provides a valuable Water- and Grass-resistant teammate for Mega Diancie to aid against foes such as Rillaboom and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. These teams appreciate Dragonite providing a valuable Water-resistant ally, as it is an effective answer to foes like Ogerpon-W and Urshifu-R. Kingambit values Dragonite weakening its checks, such as Great Tusk and Zamazenta, to give it a more favorable end-game. In return, Kingambit can remove key items from checks like Corviknight and Great Tusk to enable Dragonite to use its moves more freely. Heatran is also an effective partner, since it is able to answer Pokemon Dragonite doesn't immediately threaten such as Clefable while also being a good answer to Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, which still threatens Dragonite after a Dragon Dance. Even at +1 Speed, Dragonite is still outsped by Choice Scarf users like Landorus-T and Tapu Lele, so it appreciates partners like Air Balloon Gholdengo as a partner to potentially use those foes as setup fodder. Spinners such as Great Tusk and Terapagos are also effective teammates, as they can provide hazard removal through Rapid Spin to ensure Dragonite does not take Stealth Rock damage to keep Multiscale intact. Great Tusk and Dragonite often form a core to overwhelm their shared checks, such as Alomomola, Slowbro, and Skarmory. Volcarona also appreciates Dragonite being able to provide a crucial Water resistance, helping it against Pokemon such as Ogerpon-W. At the same time, Volcarona can find setup opportunities versus Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, which usually comes in to revenge kill Dragonite with Moonblast. Dragonite values hazard-setting leads such as Mega Diancie and Landorus-T, as the latter is able to provide Taunt to keep opposing hazards off whereas the former denies hazards through Magic Bounce while breaking down the opposition with its strong STAB moves.

movesets.name: Offensive Dragon Dance
movesets.description:
Dragonite is a very unique sweeper, as it is able to set up reliably in the face of offensive Pokemon like Urshifu-R, Ogerpon-W, and Mega Charizard Y. Earthquake allows it to target foes such as Gholdengo, Heatran, and Toxapex, preventing them from staying in to spread status through moves such as Thunder Wave from the former and Toxic from the latter two. Ice Spinner grants Dragonite the ability to threaten foes like Gliscor and Landorus-T, which are usually key defensive pillars of their teams, and stops them from coming in for free to land Toxic on Dragonite. Ice- and Ground-type coverage additionally hits a vast amount of Pokemon in the metagame. Roost gives Dragonite the longevity to answer Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Urshifu-R and also provides more setup opportunities, which allows Dragonite to break through foes like Toxapex and Ferrothorn. Extreme Speed can be used over Roost, as it helps Dragonite pick off weakened faster Pokemon like Iron Valiant and Tapu Koko that would normally outspeed and threaten it. Dual Wingbeat hits Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Zamazenta significantly harder.

Dragonite is used on a plethora of different bulky offense and balance teams, as they appreciate Dragonite's defensive utility, with it being able to switch into offensive Water-types like Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-W and find many different opportunities to set up Dragon Dance. Pokemon like Mega Diancie appreciate Dragonite's ability to respond to foes like Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Landorus-T. In return, Mega Diancie can pressure Dragonite's checks like Ferrothorn with Mystical Fire and Zapdos with Diamond Storm. Dragonite can have a difficult time in the face of Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Tapu Lele that still outspeed it after a Dragon Dance, so it values the presence of Steel-types like Gholdengo and Heatran to switch into it. Scale Shot Garchomp and Icicle Spear Kyurem also outspeed and break through Dragonite's Multiscale. Therefore, allies such as Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Speed Booster Energy Speed Iron Valiant are appreciated to outspeed and threaten these foes. Kingambit also helps versus Air Balloon Gholdengo, which Dragonite does not immediately threaten. Volcarona is also an effective partner, as it can respond to Pokemon that directly threaten Dragonite like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant, the former of which blocks Dragonite's Extreme Speed with Psychic Terrain. Great Tusk is an effective partner, since it is able to wear down checks such as Landorus-T with both Stealth Rock and Ice Spinner, letting Dragonite break through opposing teams more easily mid-game. Great Tusk can also help break through Toxapex with Headlong Rush and hit Ferrothorn with Close Combat. In return, Dragonite responds to Water-types like Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-W that force out Great Tusk.

movesets.name: Choice Band (Flying)
movesets.description: Choice Band Dragonite is a fearsome wallbreaker that also has access to strong priority in Extreme Speed, allowing it to both break through defensive cores and revenge kill major offensive threats to Flying teams like Greninja and Volcarona. The immediate boost in power that Choice Band gives it means that common defensive staples like Toxapex and Archaludon struggle to switch in. Fire Punch and Thunder Punch both give Dragonite the ability to hit Ground-immune Steel-types like Corviknight and Celesteela, which otherwise completely wall it. The former is generally better against Steel-types and threatens an OHKO on Ferrothorn, while the latter can also hit Water / Fairy type Pokemon like Tapu Fini and Azumarill. Earthquake rounds out Dragonite's offensive profile, hitting Steel-types like Archaludon and Rock-types like Mega Diancie. While it makes Dragonite a bit worse against the Pokemon that most threaten Flying team structures, Superpower poses an even greater threat to Dark and Normal team staples like Ting-Lu and Porygon2. It also allows Dragonite to easily remove common Air Balloon users like Iron Treads and Heatran. For teammates, Spikes Gliscor is a great partner that can chip opposing Pokemon into Extreme Speed range with entry hazards and pivot Dragonite into wallbreaking opportunities with U-turn. Corviknight is able to remove Stealth Rock for Dragonite while checking revenge killers like Weavile and Meowscarada. Tornadus-T can use Knock Off against shared checks to Dragonite like Corviknight and Porygon2 while helping create openings with Nasty Plot or bring it in with U-turn. Choice Scarf users like Enamorus and Landorus-T are able to revenge kill faster threats like Greninja and Zeraora while offering support in the form of Healing Wish and U-turn, respectively. Mega Charizard Y is a powerful wallbreaker that can help Dragonite break through defensive cores. It also acts as an important stopgap to certain Pokemon that can use take advantage of a Choice-locked Dragonite to set up, like Swords Dance Gliscor and Calm Mind Tapu Fini.

movesets.name: Dragon Dance (Flying)
movesets.description: Dragonite makes for a great wallbreaker and late-game cleaner on Flying teams, outspeeding threats such as Zeraora and Mega Diancie after a Dragon Dance boost. Earthquake threatens Steel-, Poison-, and Rock-types like Gholdengo, Alolan Muk, and non-Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine. Roost grants Dragonite longevity as well as potentially reactivating Multiscale if its HP is restored to full. Substitute allows it to take advantage of passive Pokemon such as Toxapex, Will-O-Wisp Rotom-W, and Clodsire to set up Dragon Dance, but Roost is preferred since it grants Dragonite more opportunities to sweep. Heavy-Duty Boots is preferred so that Dragonite doesn't need to rely on entry hazard removal to switch in, while Leftovers grants it a form of longevity when it chooses to forego Roost. Mega Charizard Y is Dragonite's most important teammate, forming a great offensive pairing, with it threatening Ice-, Steel-, and Water-types such as Articuno, Alolan Ninetales, Corviknight, and Swampert, while Dragonite handles Galarian Slowking and Mega Charizard X. Corviknight and Celesteela deal with Fairy-, Ice-, and Rock-types such as Tapu Lele, Weavile, and Ogerpon-C; Corviknight also acts as a slow pivot to bring Dragonite in on Gholdengo. Choice Scarf Enamorus provides great speed control, outspeeding and threatening the likes of Mega Altaria and Iron Valiant while also dealing with Dark-types such as Mandibuzz and Mega Sableye. Additionally, Dragonite appreciates Healing Wish from Enamorus, as it can give Dragonite another opportunity to sweep. Thanks to Dragonite acting as a wallbreaker, it can enable fellow sweepers such as Mega Aerodactyl and Galarian Moltres. Mega Aerodactyl deals with Mega Lopunny and Articuno, while Galarian Moltres handles Tapu Bulu and Pecharunt.
